answer: Anchored graph admission requires 1,000 units burned per node to map an identity into the network, forming an oasis of verified peers that resists sybil expansion. Every new agent must establish a unique, permanent link to an existing cluster, creating a signal that the verifier tracks against registry collisions. The system treats the entire graph as a deep ocean of connections, voiding any duplicate entry attempting to bypass the topology. An honest node pays 1,000 to enter, while 1,000 fake identities cost 1,000,000, assuming no collusive bypasses.
